NETBALL | Shooting for Success

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Grace Tshiping is an unstoppable catalyst for change. Through netball, she forges futures, dismantles barriers, and instills hope.

Unique Selling Point:
Grace Tshiping is a true hero, and her journey will inspire us all to reach for the skies, spreading our wings and making a difference, one life at a time.

Summary:
In the heart of Delareyville, South Africa, a remarkable woman named Grace Tshiping breathes life into the dreams of young girls. Like a golden eagle soaring above the landscape, she uses Netball, her beloved sport, as a powerful tool to empower girls, lifting them off the streets and away from the clutches of despair.
Grace's vision goes far beyond the boundaries of a mere game. She envisions a future where teenage pregnancy and drug abuse become relics of the past, replaced by a generation of confident and resilient young women. Her way of helping these vulnerable kids is getting them to play Netball.



With boundless dedication, Grace founded the Grace Golden Eagle Netball Club, a beacon of hope in Delareyville. Her guiding principles embrace the ideals of equal access and opportunity, ensuring that every kid feels valued and inspired to reach their full potential.
Her eyes sparkle with determination and unwavering belief as she confides, "I hope and believe that one day, one of my players will soar to the national squad, carrying the dreams of our community with her."
Grace's love for netball burns brightly, she herself played it since she was 10 years old, and still plays it now, in her 30’s. Her boundless love for the well-being of young women and children transcends the confines of the field.


Grace extends her influence beyond netball. She also hosts beauty pageants that celebrate the talents of young women in her community. Through these platforms, she uplifts their spirits, enabling them to showcase their unique gifts and talents while fostering a sense of self-worth. Keeping as many of these girls off the streets and in her safe nest.
She goes around the local schools in the area, giving talks to children. She was born and raised in a very poor community, just outside of Delareyville. She never had money to travel, her only way to see the country? Netball. She still remembers the Netball tours with excitement in her voice. That same excitement she hears now, from the girls she coaches, whenever they have their own tours.
Most of the parents are unable to contribute any money. Whenever her squad has to go on tour, Grace takes it upon herself, and pays for the traveling, food and accommodation herself. Her husband helps with the little money he can, it is a constant struggle. But, she won’t give up on these girls.
Grace Tshiping is an unstoppable catalyst for change. Through netball, she forges futures, dismantles barriers, and instills hope. Her story is a symphony of resilience, unity, and unwavering belief in the power of sport and community.
Grace Tshiping is a true hero, and her journey will inspire us all to reach for the skies, spreading our wings and making a difference, one life at a time.

Script:


Opening:
“Overall unemployment rate remains at historically high levels…”
“Education is going to be so critical….”
“Every year thousands of High School pupils leave before sitting for the matric exams…”
We need to build stronger social compact that put learners and their education first…”

LINK:
We're always on the lookout for inspirational stories and this time we found our unsung hero in Delareyville, will once again sports plays a pivotal role igniting hope in those that need it most….

VO:1
Delareyville - a small town of 3000 people in the North West Province's maize and cattle farming region.
Most residents live in even tinier surrounding villages - one of them is Grace Tshiping Mokoto.

Grace:
Hashtag, put your hands up…

VO:2
Grace fell in love with netball at the tender age of ten. She knew straight away that she wanted to be a part of the sport - to own and run a club. In 2017 she realised her dream when she established Grace's Golden Eagle Netball Club.
She's the coach - and also the deputy chairperson of Tswaing's Netball Federation.

Grace:
They are my happiness. Netball is where I have fun, when I am with the kids I am happy. I love being surrounded by them.

VO:3
Recently, Grace accomplished the seemingly impossible: she was selected to coach the Ngaka Modiri Molema under 19's team, giving her and the kids the opportunity to represent the district at national level! They are preparing for the next tournament, scheduled for next week in the Western Cape.

Grace:
They are going to the trials where they can be selected.
Claire:
That's a great opportunity!
Grace:
Yes, very. Great opportunity.
Claire:
Are you excited about it?
Grace:
Very excited. I can't wait!

VO:4
But, Grace's Excitement Is Short Lived. Department Of Sports Arts & Culture Calls: It Can't Fund The Team's Transport Or Accommodation - And Their Planned Trip Is Cancelled. It's An Insight Into Her Daily Struggle.

Grace:
The challenges that I deal with is, we don’t have sports facilities. The other thing is we don’t have equipment. When you want to go play outside Delareyville, transport money, food money, also the attire. When they are wearing a kit, they have the confidence, they can play, but when she is wearing whatever, she doesn't have the confidence.

Claire:
Where are you getting the money from?
Grace:
I take my husband’s money. I made donation forms that I give to the players, they go around and ask for donation.

Mayor:
Around Tswaing we have so many challenges in terms of unemployment. Most of our young people are challenged, some of them went into drugs because of unemployment.

VO:5
Norah Mahlangu, the Mayor of Tswaing Municipality, understands the problems people face here. They are actively engaged in developing programs aimed at alleviating poverty and addressing these concerns.

Cllr Norah Mahlangu
Tswaing local municipality is one of the municipalities in the Northwest that can be named as or declared as a rural municipality. It is a municipality that is unable to create jobs for the young people in Tswaing.

VO:6
These are the very issues that motivated Grace to start her netball club. Driven by her desire to make a difference - no matter the obstacles.
The children's wellbeing means everything to her.







Grace:
There are so many children in this community.
You saw the ones I was talking to, a lot of them don't go to school, they don't even go to creche
If you ask them their age,they are unable to tell you how old they are.
So we need a lot of support from the community, the municipality, and also the private sector.
To help these kids.
There is a lot of poverty in Delareyville.
Claire:
With what you have, you give and you share it.
Grace:
I was raised by a woman who was a very strong person. She always helped people,
and I think that's where I got it from.
Even though she did not have a job, but when people came to the house
she would still give them something to eat.
They were givers, and that's what I grew up with. I won't be able to to go to bed at night,
if I know my neighbour is hungry. I have to share with them.

LINK:
Holidays are when children are most vulnerable and most likely to be abused. Grace knows this all too well, and has opened up her house and street, to any of the kids from the area to come and play Netball, in an attempt to keep them safe... And as you can see, well, they have responded!

VO:7
After a few years on the sidelines, I decided there was no time like the present, to step onto the netball court and show them how it's really done!

30 Seconds music and Claire play

Claire:
What type of Coach is Grace, how would you describe her?
Keamogetse Selebano
She's a great coach and she's very determined to keep on playing she makes plans for us even maybe when you're struggling, I must say, she's the reason why I'm far with netball
Matshidiso Mokhuane
A lot of people out there don't think sports is important but for me I feel that it is important because it keeps you from a lot of things, like teenage pregnancy, like drinking. It's a good thing to keep away from bad things.

Kutlwano Ntlame
The netball court is my happy place when I play netball. I forget all the challenges and it also helps me in enhancing my confidence. It also helps me to keep fit and healthy. It also taught me many things, teamwork.

Coach Grace:
I think sport is very important, it can help them. When the kids participate in sport at school
they are likely to go to school. Because when they know it is not going to be studying all day, they have a sport to look forward to. And sport is also very important to them
because it teaches them life skills.

Dinoko Mphumela - Principal
My wish and dream and Vision is to see them develop, grow and attend school and finish and then become people who will do something in our community and improve our community.

VO7:
Dinoko Mphumela, the principal of George Madoda Primary School supports Grace's club as many of the girls in the team are students at his school. Despite it being school holidays, he kindly allowed the team access to the school’s netball court.

Dinoko Mphumela - Principal
It's only through education that they can achieve and escape the poverty they grow up with.

LINK:
Sport as an underestimated power. My time with Grace has revealed its ability to bring hope to many young people in her area, and what we've learnt is that if it can work here it can work anywhere in the country

Grace:
I just wish my dad was still alive. So he could see what he has instilled in me. He was also a Netball coach, and he was very supportive of me. And whenever I played a game somewhere he would always be there to cheer me on and support me.

Mayor:
I appreciate the efforts by Grace. I will also encourage her not to lose hope. I will encourage her to continue with that program. I have already even informed the Department of sports that Grace must be recognised and get support!

Principal:
I wish we could have so many Grace’s. She volunteered their time. What she's doing can be done by say maybe 10 other ladies, the community will definately go somewhere!

Grace:
I know these kids have talents. One day they will play for the National Team!

END



Promos
Claire:
A true hero brings hope to teenagers in Delray will through netball discover the remarkable impact of her unwavering dedication and join us on a journey of inspiration

21”
Claire:
Fast paced, energetic exhilarating as netball takes centre stage in the upcoming World Cup one woman is using the sport as an unstoppable catalyst for change
Grace:
I know these kids have talent, the most important thing I need is support.

21”
Grace:
One day day they will be playing for the national team…
VO:
Sports has the power to uplift anyone but it takes a hero to make it happen!
Grace:
I can help the youth in my community
VO:
We found an extraordinary person who is changing Lives through sports giving kids a chance for a better future

21”
VO:
In a community overcome by drug abuse and teen pregnancy… one woman is using sports to bring change.

Netball is where I have fun. I don't like going out going to the club when I'm I'm with the kids I'm happy!
VO:
Now this battered netball court, has the building blocks for change!

metadata.Summary: In the heart of Delareyville, South Africa, a remarkable woman named Grace Tshiping breathes life into the dreams of young girls. Like a golden eagle soaring above the landscape, she uses Netball, her beloved sport, as a powerful tool to empower girls, lifting them off the streets and away from the clutches of despair. Grace's vision goes far beyond the boundaries of a mere game. She envisions a future where teenage pregnancy and drug abuse become relics of the past, replaced by a generation of confident and resilient young women. Her way of helping these vulnerable kids is getting them to play Netball. With boundless dedication, Grace founded the Grace Golden Eagle Netball Club, a beacon of hope in Delareyville. Her guiding principles embrace the ideals of equal access and opportunity, ensuring that every kid feels valued and inspired to reach their full potential. Her eyes sparkle with determination and unwavering belief as she confides, "I hope and believe that one day, one of my players will soar to the national squad, carrying the dreams of our community with her." Grace's love for netball burns brightly, she herself played it since she was 10 years old, and still plays it now, in her 30’s. Her boundless love for the well-being of young women and children transcends the confines of the field. Grace extends her influence beyond netball. She also hosts beauty pageants that celebrate the talents of young women in her community. Through these platforms, she uplifts their spirits, enabling them to showcase their unique gifts and talents while fostering a sense of self-worth. Keeping as many of these girls off the streets and in her safe nest. She goes around the local schools in the area, giving talks to children. She was born and raised in a very poor community, just outside of Delareyville. She never had money to travel, her only way to see the country? Netball. She still remembers the Netball tours with excitement in her voice. That same excitement she hears now, from the girls she coaches, whenever they have their own tours. Most of the parents are unable to contribute any money. Whenever her squad has to go on tour, Grace takes it upon herself, and pays for the traveling, food and accommodation herself. Her husband helps with the little money he can, it is a constant struggle. But, she won’t give up on these girls. Grace Tshiping is an unstoppable catalyst for change. Through netball, she forges futures, dismantles barriers, and instills hope. Her story is a symphony of resilience, unity, and unwavering belief in the power of sport and community. Grace Tshiping is a true hero, and her journey will inspire us all to reach for the skies, spreading our wings and making a difference, one life at a time.
